propositions: A blocked writer cannot identify whether a lock holder is a compaction sweep and whether it is safe to interrupt, receiving only a bare pid in the timeout message.
The compaction sweep operation is interruptible without data loss because a skipped sweep is a no-op and the next trigger re-folds events, but this guarantee is not communicated to operators.
An ambient operation label carried through contextvars from sweep entry points can reach _owner_stamp and stamp the lock file with an op= field without modifying individual acquisition call sites.
The lock timeout error message must render the op= label and append a remedy text when the holder is identified as a known interruptible operation like compact-sweep.
The v2 lock stamp format must remain colon-free for backward compatibility, with the op= label sanitized to a single token and never consulted by staleness/reclamation logic.
